    Dune Meadows IV: Design-Aware Multivariate Dispersion

    dune-dispersion.Rmd

    PERMANOVA tests location in multivariate space. PERMDISP asks a different question: do groups have different average distances from their own center? The two results should be reported together when dispersion differences could complicate a location effect.

    A balanced subset of vegan::dune

    The NM and SF management groups each contain six sites, which places this example inside Phase 8’s balanced one-way envelope.

    data(dune, dune.env, package = "vegan")
selected <- dune.env$Management %in% c("NM", "SF")
dune_community <- dune[selected, ]
dune_design_data <- droplevels(dune.env[selected, , drop = FALSE])
bray <- vegan::vegdist(dune_community, method = "bray")
table(dune_design_data$Management)
#> 
#> NM SF 
#>  6  6

    The location and dispersion tests use the same Bray–Curtis dissimilarity but have different response hypotheses.

    location <- permanova_oneway(
  bray,
  dune_design_data$Management,
  permutations = 999,
  seed = 20260718,
  engine = "projection"
)
design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ Management, dune_design_data, bray
)
dispersion <- permanova_dispersion(
  design,
  term = "Management",
  type = "median",
  permutations = 999,
  seed = 20260718
)
location$table
#>       term df        ss        ms pseudo_f p_perm
#> 1    group  1 0.7575728 0.7575728 3.425694  0.005
#> 2 Residual 10 2.2114434 0.2211443       NA     NA
#> 3    Total 11 2.9690162        NA       NA     NA
dispersion$table
#>         term df         ss         ms  pseudo_f p_perm
#> 1 Management  1 0.02578244 0.02578244 0.9172607  0.368
#> 2   Residual 10 0.28108080 0.02810808        NA     NA
dispersion$group_distances
#>        NM        SF 
#> 0.4514048 0.3587002

    Agreement with vegan::betadisper

    The geometry and observed statistic match the reference implementation. Given an identical permutation matrix, the complete residual-permutation statistic vector also matches; that stronger invariant is part of the package tests.

    vegan_dispersion <- vegan::betadisper(
  bray,
  dune_design_data$Management,
  type = "median"
)
max(abs(dispersion$distances - vegan_dispersion$distances))
#> [1] 1.791434e-11
c(
  distmer = dispersion$test$statistic,
  vegan = unname(anova(vegan_dispersion)["Groups", "F value"])
)
#>   distmer     vegan 
#> 0.9172607 0.9172607

    Bray–Curtis can be non-Euclidean. Phase 8 retains positive and negative PCoA axes when calculating pseudo-Euclidean distances to a center; it never drops negative eigenvalues silently.

    dispersion$geometry[c(
  "positive_axes", "negative_axes", "negative_count", "zero_clamped"
)]
#> $positive_axes
#> [1] 8
#> 
#> $negative_axes
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $negative_count
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $zero_clamped
#> [1] 0
head(dispersion$eigenvalues)
#> [1] 1.07220146 0.86532716 0.42794658 0.32496825 0.15363993 0.07731521

    A balanced mixed-design companion

    Here treatment is assigned to whole sites and three samples are collected from each site. The dispersion response is tested over residual site variation, and whole sites—not individual samples—are exchangeable.

    sampling <- expand.grid(
  replicate = factor(1:3), site = factor(1:8)
)
sampling$treatment <- factor(
  ifelse(as.integer(sampling$site) <= 4, "reference", "restored")
)
set.seed(20260718)
site_effect <- matrix(rnorm(8 * 10, sd = 0.25), 8, 10)
residual_scale <- ifelse(sampling$treatment == "restored", 0.45, 0.3)
linear <- 1.4 + site_effect[sampling$site, ] +
  matrix(rnorm(nrow(sampling) * 10), ncol = 10) * residual_scale
community <- matrix(
  rpois(length(linear), lambda = exp(linear)),
  nrow(sampling), 10
)
mixed_bray <- vegan::vegdist(community, method = "bray")
mixed_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment + (1 | site), sampling, mixed_bray
)
mixed_dispersion <- permanova_dispersion(
  mixed_design,
  term = "treatment",
  permutations = 999,
  seed = 20260718
)
mixed_dispersion$table
#>                      term df          ss          ms  pseudo_f p_perm
#> 1               treatment  1 0.001945212 0.001945212 0.4506073  0.517
#> 2 site within fixed model  6 0.025901200 0.004316867        NA     NA
mixed_dispersion$test[c(
  "exchangeable_units", "permutation_strata", "permutation_algorithm"
)]
#> $exchangeable_units
#> [1] "site"
#> 
#> $permutation_strata
#> [1] "unrestricted whole plots"
#> 
#> $permutation_algorithm
#> [1] "full-model residual permutation of whole plots"

    Interpretation and boundary

    Spatial medians are the default because the pinned small-sample validation is better calibrated than the centroid sensitivity. type = "centroid" remains available for comparison with earlier PERMDISP workflows.

    Phase 8 requires exactly one categorical fixed main effect, equal target-group sizes, and one of the validated balanced random structures. A significant result indicates different average distances to group centers and may complicate a PERMANOVA location result. A non-significant result does not prove equal multivariate distributions or unrestricted exchangeability.
